Record Class ShotGate.Tolerances

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
frc.robot.subsystems.ShotGate.Tolerances
Record Components:
hoodStartDeg - largest hood error to start a volley at, degrees
hoodKeepDeg - largest hood error to keep feeding at, degrees
hoodStartMaxDegPerSec - fastest the hood may be moving to start a volley, deg/s
aimKeepScale - how much wider the keep-feeding heading tolerance is than the start one
settleSeconds - how long every start check must hold before the volley starts
timeoutSeconds - how long the gate may hold a launch before feeding anyway
Enclosing class:
ShotGate
public static record ShotGate.Tolerances(double hoodStartDeg, double hoodKeepDeg, double hoodStartMaxDegPerSec, double aimKeepScale, double settleSeconds, double timeoutSeconds) extends Record

  • Method Details

    • fm

      public static ShotGate.Tolerances fm()
      FM's numbers. Each is the offseason bot's, or FM's own constant, unless noted; CALIBRATE against Shot/* and ShotLog/* from the first practice session.
      • Hood 1 deg to start, 3 to keep. The offseason bot started at 0.5; FM's hood moves on Motion Magic toward a target that moves with distance while shooting on the move, and the model moves about 0.5 deg per 15 cm, so 1 deg is about 30 cm of range.
      • And the hood moving under 20 deg/s to start. In the sim the hood overshoots a 3.5 deg move by 3 deg and swings back through the target at 35 deg/s; without this the volley opened on the way through, then chopped when the overshoot passed 3 deg. Shooting on the move the target itself moves a few deg/s at most.
      • Heading keep tolerance twice the start one (the offseason bot's turret was 2 to 6).
      • Settle 0.04 s: the offseason bot's three 20 ms loops, rounded to FM's 10 ms loop.
      • Timeout 1.0 s: longer than a spin-up from idle plus a half turn, short enough that an auto's 2.5 s launch window still has 1.5 s of feeding in the worst case.
      Returns:
      the tolerances
